title: tmux sesh picker popup wastes most of its height — only ~2 items visible
description:
## Symptom

Hitting `<prefix> t` opens the sesh picker popup, but only ~2 list entries render below the filter prompt — the rest of the popup is empty space. All sessions are reachable by pressing the down arrow (the list pages), so the data is there; it just doesn't fill the popup.

Screenshot: popup is roughly 12–13 rows tall, but only `dotfiles/procs` and `gruppo` show; `Home 🏠`, `strava-timeline`, `watch-face-test` are below the visible area.

## Two contributing bugs

### 1. Height calc uses different flags than the picker

`.config/tmux/bin/tmux-sesh-picker:19` counts entries with:

```sh
sesh list -c -t -T
```

…but the picker itself runs with `-i -d -H -c -t -T` (the `-d` dedupes, `-H` hides attached sessions). On my machine that's 9 vs 5:

```text
$ sesh list -c -t -T          | wc -l   # 9
$ sesh list -i -d -H -c -t -T | wc -l   # 5
```

`CLAUDE.md` even codifies the rule the wrapper is breaking:

> Sources for `sesh list` MUST mirror the `sesh picker` flag set so the count matches what fzf will display.

Effect: popup is sized for 9 items even when only 5 will show — but this only over-sizes by ~4 rows, so it isn't the main cause of the empty space.

### 2. sesh's bubbletea TUI doesn't expand to fill the popup

`sesh picker` is a bubbletea TUI (not an fzf wrapper), and its list component appears to render at a small fixed height regardless of available rows. The wasted space below the items in the screenshot is sesh's chrome, not our popup miscalc.

title: Decide how to handle lnav runtime files in working tree
description:
After running `lnav`, the following untracked files appear in `git status`:

- `.config/lnav/configs/default/` — lnav's built-in config bundle, materialized on first run
- `.config/lnav/formats/default/` — built-in log formats (syslog, access_log, etc.)
- `.config/lnav/log_metadata.db` — SQLite DB for per-file bookmarks/parser state
- `.config/lnav/view-info-*.ts*.ppid*.json` — per-session view state keyed by PID

These are runtime/per-machine artifacts that lnav writes alongside the tracked `configs/installed/` and `formats/installed/` directories (which are what we deliberately commit, per `CLAUDE.md`).

## Options

1. **Add `.gitignore` entries** to silence them (likely the right call, mirrors the pattern used for `tmux/plugins/`, `nvim/lazy|mason|site/`, `worktrunk/approvals.toml`, etc.).
2. **Move tracked content into a sibling repo dir** and symlink only what's tracked, so the untracked runtime files live outside the symlinked tree. More invasive; probably overkill.
3. **Leave as-is** and rely on `git status -uno` discipline. Not great — defeats the purpose of a clean status.

## Suggested resolution

Add to `.gitignore`:
```
# lnav runtime state — built-in configs/formats are auto-materialized; per-session state is per-machine
.config/lnav/configs/default/
.config/lnav/formats/default/
.config/lnav/log_metadata.db
.config/lnav/view-info-*.json
.config/lnav/crash/
.config/lnav/staging/
```

Defer to a later session to decide and implement.

title: Bootstrap: install JetBrainsMono Nerd Font via Brewfile cask
description:
The dotfiles setup is pinned to **Solarized + JetBrainsMono Nerd Font everywhere** (per `CLAUDE.md`'s "Conventions — don't drift from these"), but the font itself is currently a manual prerequisite — referenced only in `README.md` prose, not present in `Brewfile`, not detected by `bootstrap.sh`.

That gap means a fresh machine can run `bootstrap.sh` cleanly while still missing the foundational font, with no warning. Anything that depends on Nerd Font glyphs (powerline arrows in the prompt, file-type icons in eza/lf, the upcoming `modern-reminder` lightbulb glyph, etc.) silently degrades to tofu/missing-glyph.

## Proposed change

Add one line to `Brewfile`:

```ruby
cask "font-jetbrains-mono-nerd-font"
```

That's it. `bootstrap.sh`'s existing `brew bundle check` step will then flag the font as missing on a fresh machine — matching the "Brewfile is report-only" convention.

## Why a cask works here

- Homebrew folded `homebrew/cask-fonts` into the main cask repo; no extra tap needed.
- macOS-only, but `Brewfile` is already mac-shaped (Ghostty.app, etc.), so no portability regression.
- Zero install side-effects from `bootstrap.sh` itself — it only reports, never installs.

## Out of scope

- Don't bundle with unrelated tool changes (per the convention reiterated in #48).
- README update is optional — the existing line ("all in Solarized + JetBrainsMono Nerd Font") still reads fine; the Brewfile entry is the discoverability fix.

title: wt pre-remove: rsync all gitignored files back to primary, not just .superpowers/.autonomo
description:
## Problem

The current `[pre-remove]` save-shared hook in `.config/worktrunk/config.toml` only rsyncs two named directories (`.superpowers/` and `.autonomo/`) from the worktree back to the primary repo on `wt remove`. Any other gitignored content created during the worktree's lifetime is dropped.

Concrete example: `plugins/autonomo/skills/autonomo-workspace/` (eval iteration runs, used by the autonomo plugin under `gruppo`) is gitignored. If a worktree is removed before that workspace is manually copied out, it's lost. Each new gitignored artefact directory needs another hook edit.

## Proposal

Replace the named-directory loop with `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard` piped to rsync. Git already knows what's ignored — let it drive the file list. Add an explicit exclude list for known-bulky artefacts (build outputs, dependency caches) that shouldn't migrate to primary.

Current hook (`.config/worktrunk/config.toml:264-265`):

\`\`\`toml
[pre-remove]
save-shared = "for d in .superpowers .autonomo; do [ -d \"\$d\" ] || continue; rsync -a --ignore-existing \"\$d/\" \"{{ primary_worktree_path }}/\$d/\"; done"
\`\`\`

Proposed:

\`\`\`toml
[pre-remove]
save-shared = "git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z | rsync -a --ignore-existing --from0 --files-from=- --exclude='node_modules/' --exclude='target/' --exclude='dist/' --exclude='.next/' ./ {{ primary_worktree_path }}/"
\`\`\`

## Why this approach

- **No per-path maintenance.** New gitignored dir

title: Step 5: Drop oh-my-zsh, load powerlevel10k directly
description:
## Problem

After the previous step empties `plugins=()`, OMZ contributes only:

- `ZSH_THEME` loader (sources powerlevel10k).
- `compinit` bootstrap.
- A small set of opinionated zstyles / history options / shell options.

That's ~3 lines of equivalent zsh. OMZ adds ~30–80 ms of startup that's no longer buying anything.

This step is *not* the prompt swap — p10k continues to render. It's purely the framework removal, isolated from the bigger Starship rewrite (next step) so each can be reverted independently if it breaks.

## Proposal

Replace this block in `.zshrc:1-12`:

```zsh
if [[ -r "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/p10k-instant-prompt-${(%):-%n}.zsh" ]]; then
  source "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/p10k-instant-prompt-${(%):-%n}.zsh"
fi

export ZSH="$HOME/.oh-my-zsh"
ZSH_THEME="powerlevel10k/powerlevel10k"
plugins=()
source "$ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh"
```

with a direct equivalent:

```zsh
# p10k instant prompt (unchanged — must stay near top)
if [[ -r "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/p10k-instant-prompt-${(%):-%n}.zsh" ]]; then
  source "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/p10k-instant-prompt-${(%):-%n}.zsh"
fi

# Completion bootstrap (was provided by OMZ)
autoload -Uz compinit && compinit

# Powerlevel10k theme (was sourced via $ZSH_THEME)
source /opt/homebrew/share/powerlevel10k/powerlevel10k.zsh-theme
```

Cleanup:

- `Brewfile`: add `brew "powerlevel10k"`.
- Other machine + this one: `rm -rf ~/.oh-my-zsh` after verifying.
- Verify each `.config/zsh/*.zsh` module still works

title: Step 6: Migrate prompt from powerlevel10k to Starship
description:
## Problem

[Powerlevel10k is on life support](https://hashir.blog/2025/06/powerlevel10k-is-on-life-support-hello-starship/) — the author has stated publicly that no new features are planned, and most bug reports go unanswered. The theme still works, but upstream is effectively frozen as of ~2024.

After steps 1–5 (mise replaces nvm/rbenv/direnv; OMZ removed), the only p10k-specific feature still in active use is **instant prompt**. Everything else (segments, transient prompt, multiline frame, custom project-context segment) ports cleanly to Starship.

## Proposal

`brew install starship`. Author `.config/starship.toml` (symlinked to `~/.config/starship.toml` via `bootstrap.sh`) porting today's p10k decisions.

Replace the p10k instant-prompt + theme-load block at the top of `.zshrc` with:

```zsh
eval "$(starship init zsh)"
```

`starship.toml` should cover:

- **Solarized palette** via `[palettes.solarized_dark]` + `palette = "solarized_dark"`. Use the same hex codes already pinned in tmux/btop/lnav configs (`#002b36`, `#fdf6e3`, etc.).
- **Segments** matching today's p10k list: `directory git_branch git_status status cmd_duration jobs custom.mise time`. Note: no `direnv` segment after step 3.
- **Custom `[custom.project_path]` module** replicating `_p9k_project_context` from `.config/zsh/prompt.zsh`:
  - `command = "..."` — bash that does the `$PROJECTS_HOME` collapse.

title: 🧰 ccstatusline: install via mise to stop npx ESM resolve races in Claude Code hooks
description:
## 🐛 Problem

Claude Code's `PreToolUse:Skill` and `UserPromptSubmit` hooks both run
`npx -y ccstatusline@latest --hook` (declared in `~/.claude/settings.json`).
That command intermittently fails with:

```
Failed with non-blocking status code: node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:271
```

The error is **non-blocking** — sessions keep working, the statusline just
fails to render that one time — but the noise lands in the transcript.

## 🔍 Root cause

Structural to the `npx -y <pkg>@latest` pattern, not a bug in ccstatusline
itself (`ccstatusline --hook` runs cleanly when invoked directly).

Two failure modes observed:

- **Race**: `PreToolUse:Skill` and `UserPromptSubmit` fire close in time;
  both invocations try to populate the same `~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/` cache
  bucket. One wins, the other loads a half-written
  `node_modules/ccstatusline/` whose ESM imports can't resolve.
- **Stale partial cache**: a prior `npx -y` was interrupted (long sessions
  get SIGTERM'd) and left a `_npx` bucket missing `dist/` or
  `node_modules/`. The next hook fire reuses the broken cache entry.

`@latest` also forces a registry round-trip and potential re-install on
every daily ccstatusline release.

## 🛠️ Proposed fix

Match the existing `mmdc` pattern: install ccstatusline globally via mise,
call it directly from hooks.

1. Add to `mise.global.toml`:

   ```toml
   [tools]
   "npm:ccstatusline" = "latest"
   ```

2. Document in README: edit `~/.claude/settings.json` so both
   ccstatusline hook

title: 🐛 messages table has no UNIQUE constraint — re-parsing inserts duplicate rows
description:
## Bug

The `messages` table schema has no UNIQUE constraint on `(session_id, ts)`. If a JSONL file is re-parsed from offset 0 (e.g. after `ccpulse index --rebuild`, or a file offset tracking bug), the same assistant turn is inserted a second time without conflict.

## Evidence

Scanning all JSONL files against the current DB:
- 183 duplicate `(session_id, ts)` pairs across all history
- 77 files affected
- ~0.18% token overcount

## Fix

1. Add `UNIQUE(session_id, ts)` to the `messages` table in `schema.sql`
2. Change `INSERT INTO messages` in `cache.go` to `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO messages` so re-parses are idempotent

## Schema migration

Existing DBs won't have the constraint. Two options:
- Bump `SchemaVersion` and add an `ALTER TABLE` / recreate step
- Or just let `ccpulse index --rebuild` create a clean DB with the new schema (document this in the `--rebuild` help text)

## Affected files

- `pkg/cache/schema.sql` — add UNIQUE constraint
- `pkg/cache/cache.go` — `InsertMessages`, change INSERT to INSERT OR IGNORE

title: feat: backfill cache gap on startup (startup index pass)
description:
## Problem

The watcher only runs while the TUI is open. Any `.jsonl` writes that happen while ccpulse is closed create a gap in the cache. On relaunch, that gap is never backfilled unless:

- The user manually runs `ccpulse index`, or
- Each affected file gets a new write event (which triggers a tail from the stored offset)

Sessions that finished while ccpulse was closed and are never reopened stay missing permanently.

## Desired behaviour

- **First run** (empty `files` table): full scan of all `.jsonl` files from byte 0 — equivalent to `ccpulse index`
- **Subsequent runs** (`files` table has offsets): tail each file from its last known offset — only the gap since last close gets parsed

## Implementation idea

On `runTUI` startup, before handing off to the watcher, walk `projectsRoot` and for each `.jsonl`:

1. `cache.GetFile(path)` → get stored offset
2. If offset == 0 (unseen): full parse
3. If offset > 0: `parse.ParseFromOffsetWithErrors(path, slug, offset, lastLine)` → insert new messages → update offset

This is exactly what the watcher does per-file on each write event — the startup pass just applies it eagerly to every file instead of waiting for a write trigger.

The watcher then takes over from the up-to-date offsets, with no gap.

## Notes

- Should run in a goroutine so it doesn't block the TUI from rendering
- Progress could be shown in the TUI (e.g. "indexing…" in the header) or silently — needs brainstorming
- `ccpulse index` can remain as a manual full-reb

title: ⚡ Reduce SQLite round-trips during Backfill enumeration
description:
## 📋 Context

Surfaced in [PR #15 review](https://github.com/martinciu/ccpulse/pull/15). `Backfill.Run` (`pkg/ingest/backfill.go:65-87`) walks the entire JSONL tree synchronously and, for each file, calls `Cache.GetFile(p)` to decide whether to enqueue it:

```go
_ = filepath.WalkDir(b.Ingester.ProjectsRoot, func(p string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
    ...
    _, offset, _, found, _ := b.Ingester.Cache.GetFile(p)
    if found && offset == info.Size() {
        return nil
    }
    entries = append(entries, entry{path: p, mtime: info.ModTime()})
    return nil
})
```

For a tree with N files, this is N SQLite round-trips before any progress callback fires. Typical Claude Code users have hundreds of files (fine), but power users with thousands of historical sessions may see noticeable startup latency before the indicator appears.

## 🎯 Proposal options

1. **Batch-load file cursors up front:** one `SELECT path, offset FROM files` query into a `map[string]int64`, then look up in-memory inside the visitor.
2. **Stream entries through a channel:** start processing first files while the walk is still in progress (loses strict mtime ordering — the first batch is "whatever WalkDir hands us first," not strictly newest).
3. **Document expected scale:** add a comment noting this is O(N) SQLite calls and tune only when someone reports slowness.

Option 1 is cheapest to implement and keeps mtime ordering intact. Recommend that.

## ✅ Acceptance

- [ ] Backfill enumeration does ≤ 1

title: 🛡️ Harden sqlite3 .backup quoting in seed-dev.sh
description:
## 🎯 Problem

\`scripts/seed-dev.sh\` runs:

\`\`\`bash
sqlite3 \"\$src\" \".backup '\$dst'\"
\`\`\`

\`\$dst\` is interpolated into a sqlite3 dot-command string. If \`\$dst\` contains a single quote, the SQL string breaks open. \`\$dst\` is built from \`XDG_CACHE_HOME\`, which a user could plausibly set to a path with a quote (e.g., \`/Users/o'malley/.cache\`).

## 🚨 Failure mode

- **Most likely:** sqlite3 prints a syntax error and the cp fallback kicks in. Annoying, recoverable.
- **Theoretical worst case:** a malicious or malformed \`XDG_CACHE_HOME\` could inject SQL via the \`.backup\` string. Real exploitation requires the user to control \`XDG_CACHE_HOME\` for an attacker, which is unusual — but defensive coding is free.

## 🛠 Approach

Standard SQL escaping: double any single quotes in \`\$dst\` before interpolation.

\`\`\`bash
local dst_escaped=\"\${dst//\\'/\\'\\'}\"
sqlite3 \"\$src\" \".backup '\$dst_escaped'\"
\`\`\`

Or pipe the command via stdin (still needs the same escaping, no real win).

## ✅ Acceptance

- [ ] \`seed-dev.sh\` survives a \`XDG_CACHE_HOME\` value containing a single quote.
- [ ] Add a Go shell-out test in \`scripts/seed_dev_test.go\` that exercises a quoted-path edge case.

## 📝 Notes

Real-world risk on the maintainer's setup is essentially zero (no quote in the home path). This is purely defensive.

## 🔗 Refs

- PR #40 introduced \`scripts/seed-dev.sh\`.
- Found during self-review of PR #40.

description:
Umbrella issue for **audit items #4 + #5**, scoped to land in a single PR. The two items are tightly coupled — shipping the WAL pragmas (#5) without the rebuild fix (#4) introduces a corruption foot-gun on the next schema bump, and shipping #4 without #5 is mostly inert.

## 🎯 Problem

Two related gaps in `pkg/cache/cache.go:Open` and the rebuild paths.

### Audit #5 — no WAL / busy_timeout / pool tuning

`Open` runs with SQLite defaults:

description:
## 🎯 Problem

`pkg/parse/parse.go:55` and `pkg/parse/tail*.go:26` use `bufio.Scanner` with
the default 64 KiB buffer (or the explicitly-bumped 1 MiB buffer in the tail
path). When a JSONL line exceeds the buffer, `Scanner.Scan()` returns false
with `err == bufio.ErrTooLong`.

The current ingest path treats this as "scanner is done" and resets — but by
the time `ErrTooLong` surfaces, the **byte cursor in the `files` table has
already advanced** past every line the scanner *did* read in this batch. The
oversized line, plus all the good lines that landed in the same buffer pass
before it, never make it into `messages`. The cursor sits past them. The next
fs event picks up from after the oversized line. Those messages are gone from
cost accounting forever.

## 🚨 Failure mode

The tool's whole pitch is "trustworthy local quota counter, accurate enough
to compare against Anthropic's billing." Silent drift breaks that pitch:

- **Cumulative under-counting.** Every oversized line in any transcript
  silently evicts itself plus a tail of prior good lines. The user has no
  signal — the TUI just shows a number that drifts low vs. their actual
  Anthropic usage by an amount they can't account for.
- **Worse on busy days.** Long lines are likelier on heavy-tool-use turns
  (giant tool results, base64-embedded screenshots, full-file Read outputs).
  Heavy days are exactly the days users most want accurate numbers.
- **Hidden by design.** No log entry, no doctor warning, no error in the TU

Two leaf render functions in `pkg/tui/model.go` hand-roll layout math (centering, right-alignment) that lipgloss has built-in primitives for. Replacing them removes ~17 lines net and one source of width-math bugs (the `h == 1` edge case in the placeholder).

## 🔧 Change 1 — `emptyPlaceholder` → `lipgloss.Place`

**Location:** `pkg/tui/model.go:291-308`

Current: builds an `[]string` of `h` rows, picks the middle index, prepends `strings.Repeat(" ", pad)` to center the message on that one row, then `strings.Join` with `\n`.

Replacement: one call to `lipgloss.Place(w, h, lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center, msg)` — purpose-built for centering a block inside a `w×h` box.

## 💡 Why

Two correctness gaps in the pricing layer, related closely enough to ship together:

1. **No record of which `pricing.json` version costed each row.** `cost_usd_estimate` is computed once at insert time in `pkg/cache/cache.go:192` and never updated. description:
## 🔍 Summary

`ntcharts` v0.5.1's `DrawBrailleAll` composites multiple datasets into a single canvas with **last-writer-wins per cell** — only the rune dots get OR'd; the cell style is overwritten. Where the 5h and 7d lines pass through the same 2×4 braille cell, the merged rune is colored green (5h, drawn last due to alphabetical sort of `"7d"` < `"default"`), masquerading the 7d line as green in those stretches.

## 📷 Repro

Any chart view where both series sit near the same quota fraction for an extended span — e.g. both near 100% remaining for the older half of the window. Visible result: the 7d (pink) line appears green over those stretches, then "switches back" to pink where the two lines separate in y.

> Attach the screenshot from the original report here when filing — see `/Users/martinciu/.claude/image-cache/f125b969-c995-4159-a633-fbcebc1fae03/1.png` locally.

## 🧭 Root cause

1. `timeserieslinechart.DrawBrailleAll` (`timeserieslinechart.go:336`) does `sort.Strings(names)`. ASCII `'7' = 0x37 < 'd' = 0x64`, so `"7d"` draws first, `"default"` (5h) second.

3. Net effect: shared cells get 5h's green. The 7d line appears intermittently green wherever its dot positions collide with 5h's.

- Document the silent-no-op behaviour. Rejected: unusual CLI shape, and the error message is more useful than a comment in a manpage no one reads.

`cmd/ccpulse/index.go:57` calls `RemoveWithSiblings(dbPath)` from
`ccpulse index --rebuild` without checking whether another `ccpulse`
process already has the cache open. There is no advisory file lock
around `state.db` — the `flock` in `pkg/anthro/usage.go:223` covers
`usage.json.lock` only.

User runs the TUI in one terminal, then `ccpulse index --rebuild` in

   when it closes its handle.

ate their TUI's in-flight cache.

Brainstorm needs to choose between:

  using the cache" message if it can't acquire.
- **Coexist safely.** Defer the unlink until all readers/writers
  have closed (hard — POSIX file locks don't gate unlink).

title: 🚫 Root command silently launches TUI on typos / unknown args
description:
## 🎯 Problem

`cmd/ccpulse/main.go:79-96` builds the root with `RunE: runTUI` but
no `Args` validator. Cobra defaults to `ArbitraryArgs`, so any token
that doesn't match a subcommand name falls through to the root.

## 🚨 Failure mode

```
$ ccpulse stauts
# launches the TUI; user assumes status ran and exited silently
$ ccpulse foo bar baz
# launches the TUI, args swallowed
$ ccpulse statu --json
# launches the TUI, --json never reaches a status handler
```

Users hit this any time they misspell a subcommand. There is no
error, no usage hint, no log line.

## 🛠 Approach

Set the root's `Args` to `cobra.NoArgs`. The root has no positional
arg surface — every positional belongs to a subcommand.

## ✅ Acceptance

- [ ] `ccpulse stauts` exits non-zero with a usage error.
- [ ] `ccpulse` with no args still launches the TUI.
- [ ] Test: extra-args case asserts non-zero exit and "unknown command"
      / "accepts 0 arg(s)" in stderr.

## 🔗 Refs

- Audit umbrella: #68
- Existing pattern: every leaf subcommand already uses `cobra.NoArgs`
  (see `cobra_hygiene_test.go::TestLeafCommandsRejectExtraArgs`); the
  root is the only one missing the policy.

location runs `ccpulse recost` and silently operates on the **default**

Only `CCPULSE_CACHE_DIR` env override works.

Subcommand is `Hidden: true` so the blast radius is small, but the
inconsistency with every other subcommand is a real bug.

## 🛠 Approach

Replace `config.Load("")` with `config.Load(config.DefaultPath())` in
`recost.go:23`. Mechanical fix.

## ✅ Acceptance

- [ ] `recost` honors `cache_dir` from the user's `config.toml`.
- [ ] Test: write a config with a non-default `cache_dir`, run

title: 🔇 TUI and status silently swallow config.Load errors
description:
## 🎯 Problem

Two call sites discard the returned error from `config.Load`:

- `cmd/ccpulse/main.go:212` — `cfg, _ := config.Load(...)` (TUI)
- `cmd/ccpulse/status.go:36` — `cfg, _ := config.Load(...)` (status)

`runIndex` (`index.go:39`) handles the error correctly with
`!os.IsNotExist`; `recost` surfaces it via wrap. Only the two
flagship subcommands silently ignore it.

User's `~/.config/ccpulse/config.toml` has a typo (stray bracket,
wrong type — `retention_days = "abc"`, etc.). `BurntSushi/toml.Decode`
returns an error. Both `runTUI` and `runStatus` discard it. The
partially-populated `cfg` is used downstream; the user sees a
confusing "wrong cache directory" or "missing value" symptom instead
of the actual "parse error at line N" message they need.

At both call sites, treat `config.Load` errors that are not
`os.IsNotExist` (file absent → fine, defaults kick in) as fatal:
log + return error to cobra. Same shape as `runIndex` already uses.

- [ ] `runTUI` and `runStatus` return the wrapped `config.Load` error
      when the config file exists but is malformed.
- [ ] Both still launch with defaults when the config file is absent.
- [ ] Test: planted malformed config triggers a clear stderr message
      with the line/column from BurntSushi/toml's error.

- Audit umbrella: #68

title: 🧹 recost: align config-load error handling with other commands
description:
## 🐛 The inconsistency

Every command that calls `config.Load(config.DefaultPath())` filters
`os.IsNotExist` so a missing config file is non-fatal — the channel-aware
defaults from `pkg/config` carry the run. `recost` is the lone outlier:
it returns the raw error and aborts.

```go
// cmd/ccpulse/recost.go:23-26
cfg, err := config.Load(config.DefaultPath())
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf(\"load config: %w\", err)
}
```

Compare:

```go
// cmd/ccpulse/main.go:213-216  (runTUI)
cfg, err := config.Load(config.DefaultPath())
if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
    return fmt.Errorf(\"load config %s: %w\", config.DefaultPath(), err)
}
```

`status.go:37-40` and `index.go:38-41` follow the same `!os.IsNotExist`
pattern as `runTUI`. `doctor.go:30-31` reports the error informationally
and continues. `recost` alone bails.

## 🤔 Why it matters

Low-stakes — `recost` is a `Hidden: true` subcommand and `config.Load`
already returns populated defaults even on the file-read error, so the
fix is mechanical and the user impact is small (anyone running `recost`
on a machine without a config file gets a confusing failure instead of
a working re-cost pass against the default cache dir).

It's an unprincipled outlier in a small surface — worth tidying before
v0.1.0 so the convention is uniform across all five subcommands.

## 🩹 The fix

```go
cfg, err := config.Load(config.DefaultPath())
if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
    return fmt.Errorf(\"load config: %w\", err)
}
```

title: 🔒 secfile: open lock files with O_NOFOLLOW
description:
## 🔍 Context

Surfaced during review of #219 (cache flock implementation). `pkg/secfile/secfile.go`'s `OpenFile` is the helper used by both `pkg/anthro/usage.go`'s `acquireFetchLock` and `pkg/cache/lock.go`'s new `acquireCacheLock`.

## 🐞 Observed

`secfile.OpenFile` calls `os.OpenFile(path, O_RDWR|O_CREATE, 0600)` followed by `os.Chmod` — neither passes `O_NOFOLLOW`. A pre-existing symlink at the lock-file path would be followed: `OpenFile` opens the symlink target, and `os.Chmod` (follow-symlink semantics) chmods the target to 0600.

The 0700 parent directory (`~/.cache/ccpulse/`) contains cross-user exploitation, but a stale or hostile local symlink silently breaks mutual exclusion — `flock` then attaches to the wrong inode while real readers stay unsynchronised.

## ✅ Expected

Add `syscall.O_NOFOLLOW` to the `OpenFile` flags in `secfile.OpenFile` (or `os.Lstat` precheck). One change at the helper covers both cache- and Anthropic-fetch-locking call sites.

## 🧪 Test plan

- [ ] Unit test in `pkg/secfile`: pre-create a symlink to a sentinel target, call `OpenFile` on the symlink path, assert the call refuses with an `ELOOP`-style error (or returns the symlink-resolved fd depending on chosen semantics).
- [ ] Verify `pkg/cache` and `pkg/anthro` test suites still pass.

Refs #219.

The behaviour is correct in code but is not exercised by any test.

2. Hold `LOCK_SH` on the lock file from a fixture fd via `acquireCacheLock`.
3. Call `Open(path)`.
4. Assert `errors.Is(err, ErrLockHeld)` — the schema-mismatch dispatch releases the caller's SH and `LockedRebuild` cannot take EX while the fixture SH is held.

## 🐞 What happens

Running `ccpulse` with no subcommand in an environment where Claude Code has never run (no `~/.claude/projects` dir) exits 1 with a single context-free line:

- `runTUI` calls `watcher.New(projectsRoot)` — `cmd/ccpulse/main.go:261`.

title: 🔁 ci: claude-review self-cancels when the bot posts its progress comment
description:
## 🐞 Problem

The `Claude Review` workflow (`.github/workflows/claude-review.yml`) cancels its own in-flight review. A `@claude review` request starts the review job, then `claude-code-action` (with `track_progress: true` + `use_sticky_comment: true`) posts a **"Claude Code is working…"** progress comment. That comment fires a second `issue_comment: created` event, which joins the same concurrency group and — because of `cancel-in-progress: true` — kills the run that posted the comment.

The job-level `@claude review` guard can't prevent this: concurrency cancellation is evaluated at the **run level, before** the job `if` runs.

## 🔬 Evidence (PR #284)

| Time (2026-05-22) | Event |
|---|---|
| 18:56:07 | `@claude review` → run `26306304577` starts |
| 18:56:36 | `claude[bot]` posts the progress comment |
| 18:56:39 | progress comment fires a 2nd run `26306323422` |
| 18:56:53 | 2nd run enters `claude-review-284` group and **cancels** the running review |

The review never posted anything — it was killed ~21s in. This recurs on essentially every review.

## 🛠️ Fix

Gate `cancel-in-progress` so only human comments cancel; bot comments never do:

\`\`\`yaml
concurrency:
  group: claude-review-${{ github.event.issue.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ !endsWith(github.event.comment.user.login, '[bot]') }}
\`\`\`

This preserves the useful behaviour (a fresh `@claude review` still supersedes a stale in-progress one) while the action's own progress comment no longer self-cancels.

title: 📜 docs: add CONTRIBUTING with an explicit contribution policy
description:
## 🎯 Problem

ccpulse is a **solo-maintained, opinionated tool** with no `CONTRIBUTING` doc and no stated contribution policy. Once the repo gets public attention (around the v0.1.0 release), drive-by PRs will start arriving. Declining a PR someone has already spent hours on is awkward; far better to set expectations **up front** so nobody wastes effort.

## ✅ Desired behavior

Add a `CONTRIBUTING.md` at the repo root (GitHub auto-links it from the issue/PR creation flow) that states the contribution policy clearly — and in a friendly, non-hostile tone.

## 🤔 Decision to make

Pick the stance before writing:

- **Hard "source available, not open contribution"** — no external PRs accepted at all (à la SQLite). Maximum control, but reads as unwelcoming if not worded carefully.
- **Softer "issues welcome, PRs by prior discussion only"** *(recommended)* — bug reports and feature requests are welcome; please open an issue and agree on the approach **before** sending code. This is the far more common variant for solo projects and avoids rejecting unsolicited PRs.

## 🤔 Why

- Outright "PRs not welcome" is uncommon (~low single-digit % of repos) but legitimate and good etiquette to state explicitly rather than silently ignoring PRs.
- The softer "discuss first" gate is very common for solo-maintained, tight-scope tools and keeps the door open for bug reports.
- ccpulse is deliberately opinionated (single TUI view, no runtime git dep, etc.), so scope control matters.

title: 📊 tui: render exact per-bucket tokens + cost inside each 24h bar (hidden during animations)
description:
## 🎯 Goal

At the **24h zoom** only, print each bucket's **exact usage and cost** *inside* the bar, anchored at the top of the bar. This turns the 24h view from "relative heights + two Y ticks" into a precise per-day readout without leaving the TUI.

Requirements (from the request):

- 📍 **Placement** — drawn on top of / inside the bar (over the bar's own cells), not above it.
- 🔢 **Tokens** — rounded, compact `k` / `M` suffixes (e.g. `1.2M`, `750k`, `42k`).
- 💲 **Cost** — rounded, **no cents** (e.g. `$45`, not `$45.30`).
- 📏 **Fit the bar width** — labels must not overflow the bar; drop/elide rather than spill into the gap or neighbouring bar.

{"24h", 24 * time.Hour,  10, 2, 1},

- `buildChart` (`pkg/tui/chart.go:608`) renders bars via `ntcharts/barchart`, then joins an X-label row underneath via `renderXLabels`. There is **no in-bar annotation*

title: 🧪 Whole-app rendering-invariant test: View() fits the terminal across a state matrix
description:
## 🧪 What

Add a whole-app rendering-invariant test: drive `Model.View()` across a matrix of terminal sizes and model states and assert the output **fits the terminal** — primarily `lines(View()) ≤ m.h`. This is a reusable backstop that guards a *class* of layout regressions, independent of any single feature.

## 🎯 Why

Per-feature width tests keep missing layout breaks because they only exercise one surface in one state:

- #318 — bars row overflowed the header box and wrapped (fixed in #319).
- #320 — burn-rate row wraps and breaks the same box at ≤100 cols with an overreaching projection.

Both share one symptom — **content wraps → extra lines → broken box / overflow** — and both slipped through green CI. A single height-based invariant over the composed `View()` would have caught both as a side effect.

## 🔍 Key design note

The catching invariant is **line-count / height**, not per-line width. When content wraps, each wrapped line stays *within* `m.w` — so a "no line wider than `m.w`" check would NOT catch #318/#320. The symptom is always extra height. So assert `lines(View()) ≤ m.h`.

Account for surfaces that overflow **by design** (don't false-positive on them):

- Footer (`renderFooter`) truncates terminal-side intentionally (`model.go` comment) — it's the last line, no box to break.
- Chart body is `bubbles/viewport`-clipped, safe by construction.
- The header box is the one fixed-geometry surface where wrapping is catastrophic — that's where the tight check pays o

title: 🐛 changelog: emoji-prefixed `docs:` commits leak past the `^docs` exclude
description:
## 🐞 Problem

The GoReleaser changelog `filters.exclude` has `^docs` to keep docs commits out of release notes, but every docs commit in this repo is **emoji-prefixed** (`📊 docs:`, `📖 docs:`, `📜 docs:`). `^docs` anchors at the start of the subject, so the leading emoji means it never matches — docs commits leak into the changelog. Two even land under **Features**, since `📊` is in the Features group regexp.

Observed for a hypothetical release of `v0.1.0..HEAD`: 5 `docs:` commits (#299, #305, #326, plus the two `📊 docs:` ones) appear in the notes.

## 🔍 Root cause

`^docs` only matches a literal `docs`-at-column-0. Emoji-first commit style (`<emoji> <type>: …`) defeats the anchor. Same latent issue affects `^chore` / `^test`, but those are partly covered by the `^(🧹|🧪|📝|🙈)` emoji exclude.

## ✅ Fix

Match an optional leading emoji token before the conventional type:

```yaml
- '^(\S+\s+)?docs(:|\()'
```

This catches `docs:`, `📊 docs:`, `📖 docs:`, `📜 docs:`, and scoped `docs(readme):`, while leaving `📊 tui:` / `📊 <feature>` features and any mid-subject "docs" mention untouched. Excludes run before grouping, so the ambiguous `📊` no longer pulls docs into Features.

title: 📄 docs: document the versioning policy in CONTRIBUTING.md
description:
## 🎯 Goal

There is no written record of how ccpulse versions its releases — the decision currently lives only in conversation. Document it in `CONTRIBUTING.md` so it is canonical and not re-litigated each release.

## 📐 Policy to document

Library-style [SemVer](https://semver.org) with **minor as the release counter**:

- **Minor** (`0.1.0` → `0.2.0`) — every normal release, features + fixes bundled.
- **Patch** (`0.2.1`) — reserved for an out-of-band hotfix between releases; normally stays `0`.
- **Major** `1.0.0` — the point where the `ccpulse status --json` schema and CLI flags are declared stable.
- During `0.x`, public surfaces (`status --json` shapes, CLI flags, config keys, cache schema) may change between minor releases; breaking changes are noted in the release notes.

## 💡 Rationale

ccpulse exposes a scriptable contract (`status --json` + CLI flags drive the README’s tmux/starship status-bar recipes), so the version number should communicate compatibility for that surface — unlike app-style schemes (e.g. Claude Code) where patch is the release counter.

## 📦 Scope

Add one `## Versioning` section to `CONTRIBUTING.md`. No code changes.

title: 🧹 lint: adopt golangci-lint for code-smell, complexity, and refactor-candidate checks
description:
## 🎯 Goal

Adopt `golangci-lint` as the project's code-quality gate, replacing the bare `go vet` in `make lint`. This gives us code-smell detection, complexity/refactor-candidate flagging, and dead-code detection in a single command — and the same command can run in CI.

## 📌 Why

Today `make lint` is just `go vet ./...`, which catches correctness footguns but says nothing about smells, complexity hotspots, duplication, or refactor candidates. `golangci-lint` aggregates 100+ linters behind one config and subsumes `go vet`.

## 🔧 Proposed linters

Tuned for a small, focused codebase — avoid the noisy ones.

- **Smells / correctness:** `staticcheck`, `gocritic`, `revive`, `unparam`, `unused`
- **Complexity / refactor candidates:** `gocyclo` (or `cyclop`), `gocognit`, `funlen`, `nestif`, `dupl`
- **Keep:** `govet` (already in use), plus standard `errcheck`, `ineffassign`, `gofumpt`/`goimports`

## ✅ Tasks

- [ ] Add `.golangci.yml` with the linter set above, tuned to avoid false-positive noise
- [ ] Point `make lint` at `golangci-lint run ./...` (add `lint-fix` + `fmt` targets)
- [ ] Triage and fix (or justify-suppress with `//nolint:<linter> // reason`) the initial findings
- [ ] Wire `golangci-lint-action` into CI alongside the existing checks
- [ ] Document the new `make lint` behaviour in `CLAUDE.md`

## 🧭 Out of scope / notes

- A top-line grade (**Go Report Card** A+→F, or **SonarCloud** quality gates) could be a follow-up if we want quality trending over time — not part o
